material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted specialty millwork. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions. Specialty millwork historically received oil-based paint (semi-gloss/gloss default sheen) making adhesion primer especially critical when solvent test confirms alkyd base.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+ or oil-based coating identified. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape. Specialty millwork surfaces have high incidence of legacy alkyd coatings.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional -- skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen latex surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime -- extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke-damaged specialty surfaces. Full-surface application required -- smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Specialty surfaces with texture (beadboard grooves, panel profiles, column flutes, mantel molding) trap concentrated smoke/nicotine deposits in detail crevices. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor -- requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup -- requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Detail profiles on specialty surfaces (wainscot panels, beadboard grooves, column flutes, mantel molding, built-in shelf corners) trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure full coverage of all profile details.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged specialty surfaces. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Most common on wood ceiling surfaces in bathrooms/kitchens where steam condensation causes mildew, and wood wall panel bottoms adjacent to wet areas. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives preventing spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades. Wood ceiling in bathroom/kitchen is the most common application -- steam condensation causes mildew growth on wood surfaces. Wood wall panel bottoms in splash zones and built-in interiors in humid rooms are secondary targets.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected areas -- mildew spores may be present beyond visible damage area

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Stain/Clear Coat Conversion
material_systems.description: Aggressive bonding primer for converting previously stained or clear-coated specialty surfaces to paint. Bridges between existing non-paint finish and latex topcoat. Common on built-in bookcases, mantels, beams, and library-style wood wall panels that were originally stained or clear-coated. Full surface application mandatory -- no skip-prime option for conversion scenarios.

products.notes: Aggressive bonding formula for non-paint existing finishes (stain, lacquer, polyurethane, shellac, varnish). Full surface -- no skip-prime option for conversion. High-tannin species (red oak, white oak, mahogany, cedar) may show tannin bleed-through after first topcoat requiring shellac spot-prime treatment. Existing finish must be thoroughly deglossed before bonding primer application.

prime_scope_by_state.stain_clear_conversion: full surface prime -- mandatory, no exceptions

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic enamel for standard residential specialty surface repaint at QT3. Fast dry/recoat, non-yellowing, water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product selection as NC fine-finish millwork specs.

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product as NC millwork finish at QT3. Adequate for production work on all 7 surface types.

material_systems.notes: QT3 -- satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD SS4.1). Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential specialty surface repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling -- critical for large flat panels (wainscot, wood wall) where brush marks are highly visible. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not overwork. Vertical surfaces (columns, mantels) and overhead surfaces (beams, ceilings) are prone to sags -- apply in thin coats.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Vertical column faces and beam undersides are prone to sags with this product -- apply in thin coats. Enclosed built-in compartments retain humidity extending dry time.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Semi-gloss is traditional millwork default at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior specialty surface repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006).

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Wainscot panel SF. Previously painted surface absorbs less than bare wood. Raised panel 3D profiles add ~10% effective surface area over measured wall SF.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Wood wall panel SF. Previously painted substrate. Shiplap/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Wood ceiling panel SF. Slightly lower effective coverage than wall due to overhead application (drip, gravity working against applicator). Coffered ceilings have significantly more surface area than flat planks.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Beam LF converted to effective SF via profile width factor (3-sided box ~4 SF/LF typical). Previously painted surface. Overhead application reduces effective coverage.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Column EA -- ~25 SF equivalent per standard 8ft column (~12" perimeter x 8ft). Previously painted surface. Fluted columns have ~30% more effective surface area.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Mantel EA -- ~20 SF equivalent for standard mantel (shelf + legs + facing). Ornate mantels up to 40 SF. Previously painted surface.

ITM_BUILTIN_UNIT.notes: Built-in EA per unit. SF equivalent based on Opening Count method tier + door/drawer faces. RP surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood. S=~8SF (small cube), M=~20SF (bookshelf section), L=~40SF (large bookcase), XL=~80SF (floor-to-ceiling entertainment center).

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted specialty surfaces. Higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer (NC at 350-400 SF/gal vs RP at 375-475 SF/gal) because previously painted surfaces absorb less. Coverage consistent across surface types for primer -- complexity modifier does not significantly affect primer coverage rate.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than bare wood
Surface type complexity affects labor rate but not coverage rate significantly
Beam/column/mantel SF equivalents are typical residential sizes

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Shellac stain blocker on smoke-damaged wainscot. Lower coverage than latex primers due to higher solids content. Panel grooves and rail-stile joints trap smoke deposits requiring thorough coverage.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Shellac stain blocker on smoke-damaged wood wall. Shiplap/T&G grooves trap smoke contamination.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Shellac on smoke-damaged ceiling. Lowest coverage due to overhead application + strong solvent odor limiting work time. Coffered ceiling detail multiplies coverage difficulty. Smoke rises -- ceiling surfaces typically have heaviest contamination.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Shellac on smoke-damaged beams. Overhead application. Beam box corners trap contamination.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Shellac on smoke-damaged columns. Fluted column channels trap concentrated smoke deposits.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Shellac on smoke-damaged mantels. Mantel profiles and shelf-to-leg joints trap contamination. Fireplace proximity means mantel is typically heavily contaminated.

ITM_BUILTIN_UNIT.notes: Shellac on smoke-damaged built-in interiors. Enclosed compartments trap smoke -- shelves, dado joints, and corners require thorough coverage. Lowest coverage rate due to enclosed compartment spray overspray waste and difficulty of access. Strong solvent odor in enclosed space limits work time.

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex primers due to higher solids content and heavier required film build. Full surface application required on all smoke-damaged surfaces. Ceiling and built-in interior surfaces have lowest coverage rates due to application difficulty.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged surfaces
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Detail profiles and enclosed compartments require additional material
Ceiling surfaces have heaviest smoke contamination (smoke rises)

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Bonding primer on stain/clear coat conversion for wainscot. Full surface mandatory.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Bonding primer for library-panel or wood wall stain/clear conversion. Full surface mandatory.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Bonding primer for stained wood ceiling conversion. Overhead penalty reduces effective coverage. Full surface mandatory.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Bonding primer for stained beam conversion. Full surface mandatory. Overhead application.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Bonding primer for stained column conversion. Full surface mandatory.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Bonding primer for stained mantel conversion. Full surface mandatory. Common conversion target.

ITM_BUILTIN_UNIT.notes: Bonding primer for stained built-in conversion. Full surface mandatory. Built-in bookcases are the most common stain-to-paint conversion target. Enclosed compartments reduce effective coverage.

coverage_profiles.notes: Bonding primer for stain/clear coat to paint conversion. Coverage similar to adhesion primer (latex-based formula). Full surface application mandatory -- no skip-prime option for conversion. Ceiling and built-in surfaces have slightly lower coverage due to application difficulty.
assumptions: Full surface application mandatory for stain/clear conversion
Latex-based bonding formula -- similar coverage to adhesion primer
High-tannin species may require shellac spot-prime after first topcoat

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged wainscot. Uncommon application.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged wood wall panel bottoms. Moisture wicks at floor level.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged wood ceiling. PRIMARY target -- bathroom/kitchen steam condensation causes mildew on wood ceilings. Overhead penalty reduces effective coverage.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged beams. Uncommon -- beams not typically in wet areas.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged columns. Rare application.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged mantels. Rare application.

ITM_BUILTIN_UNIT.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on moisture-damaged built-in interiors. Built-ins in bathrooms accumulate humidity damage. Enclosed compartments reduce effective coverage.

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer (latex-based formula). Slightly thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Primary targets: wood ceiling (bathroom/kitchen) and built-in interiors (humid rooms). Beam, column, and mantel applications are rare.
assumptions: Latex formula -- similar coverage to adhesion primer
Thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness
Wood ceiling and built-in interiors are primary moisture damage targets

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Wainscot finish coat on primed/prepared surface. Raised panel adds ~10% effective surface area from 3D profile. Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overspray around frame detail.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Wood wall finish coat on primed/prepared surface. Shiplap/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area. Large flat panel areas benefit from spray for uniformity.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Wood ceiling finish coat. Overhead application reduces effective coverage by ~5-10%. Coffered ceilings have significantly more surface area -- detail profiles multiply material consumption. Spray recommended for ceilings -- brush is extremely slow overhead.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Beam finish coat on primed surface. Effective SF depends on beam profile (3-sided box). Ornate profiles add surface area. Multiple spray passes at different angles for beam undersides.

fluted.notes: Fluted channels add ~30% surface area. Material settles in channels.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Column finish coat. Column type significantly affects coverage -- fluted columns consume ~50% more material than square.

simple_shelf.notes: Simple shelf -- small surface area, higher effective coverage.

traditional.notes: Traditional assembly (shelf + legs + facing) -- standard coverage.

ornate.notes: Ornate mantel with molding profiles, corbels, columns -- extensive surface area. Material settles in detail crevices.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Mantel finish coat. Mantel type significantly affects coverage -- ornate mantels consume ~2.5x more material than simple shelf.

ITM_BUILTIN_UNIT.notes: Built-in finish coat. SF equivalent per unit tier for material planning. Deep openings have more interior surface area -- material quantity scales with depth. Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overspray inside enclosed compartments. Door/drawer fronts estimated at ~6 SF per door/drawer (face + edges).

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed/prepared specialty surfaces. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3. Substrate condition after prime is equivalent to NC -- coverage rates match NC profiles. Column type and mantel type significantly affect per-unit coverage. Ceiling overhead penalty reduces effective coverage by ~5-10%. Premium system (QT5) at 375 SF/gal vs standard/modified at 400 SF/gal per manufacturer PDS.
assumptions: Primed smooth surface -- equivalent to NC after prime
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3
Column/mantel complexity modifier affects material consumption
Spray overspray waste higher in enclosed compartments (built-in)

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags for coating identification solvent test
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials and solvent test supplies for latex vs oil-based coating identification. Specialty millwork is HIGH RISK for oil-based existing paint -- coating ID must be performed on EACH surface type present (different surfaces may have different coating histories). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner
consumables.specification: Powdered or liquid TSP concentrate, mixed per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: RP-specific surface decontamination wash. Removes hand oils, cleaning chemical residue, wax (furniture polish on built-ins), and surface contaminants from existing paint before prep. One quart of concentrate makes enough solution for ~200 SF of specialty surface wash. Especially critical for built-in interiors (accumulated furniture polish, dust, handling oils). Not used in NC (new substrate is clean). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss paint on specialty surfaces. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without mechanical sanding. Preferred for: (1) detail profiles -- gets into wainscot panel grooves, beadboard channels, column flutes, mantel molding without changing profile shape. (2) Overhead ceiling work -- less dust generation than sanding. (3) Enclosed built-in interiors -- dust containment in enclosed space. One quart covers ~150 SF of specialty surface. Not used in NC. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Mildew Biocide Solution
consumables.specification: Mildew biocide concentrate, Concrobium Mold Control or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific mildew treatment for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE on specialty surfaces. Kills active mildew before priming. Apply, allow to dry fully (24+ hrs). Primary targets: wood ceiling in bathrooms/kitchens (steam condensation), wood wall panel bottoms near wet areas, built-in interiors in humid rooms. Not used in NC (new substrate is clean). One quart covers ~100 SF of surface.

consumables.name: Fine Sanding Sponge (150-180 grit)
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, fine grit (150-180), for contour/profile sanding
consumables.notes: Preferred for deglossing and between-coat sanding on detail profiles: wainscot raised panel bevels, beadboard grooves, T&G channels, column flutes, mantel molding profiles, built-in shelf edges. Conforms to curved/profiled surfaces better than flat sandpaper. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block on flat surfaces). One sponge covers ~20 SF of profiled surface.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge (angled edges)
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for tight profile conformance
consumables.notes: Angled-edge contour sponge for tight profile areas: wainscot rail-stile joints, panel recess corners, column flute channels, mantel shelf-to-leg joints, built-in dado joints. More specialized than CON_SANDING_SPONGE_FINE -- used in tight crevices where flat sponges cannot reach.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling specialty surfaces. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint. One sheet covers ~15 SF of scrape edge feathering. Condition-gated: FAIR and POOR only.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for mechanical degloss scuff sanding on flat specialty surfaces. All tiers. One sheet per ~15 SF for mechanical degloss. Used on flat areas where rigid sanding block can reach -- detail profiles use CON_SANDING_SPONGE_FINE instead.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats. QT3 = spot sand 220 on defects only. QT4 = full surface sand 220. Also used for light sand of primer before finish. One sheet per ~15 SF for interstage sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. Thorough 320-grit sanding per FFD 15.10.3. Uniform scratch pattern required. One sheet per ~12 SF. Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-220)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects -- mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat surfaces (wainscot flat panels, wood wall flat faces, shelf faces, mantel shelf top). Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. One block per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush for specialty surface finish and primer application. One per painter per material type (primer brush + finish brush). Used for all surface types: wainscot detail, wood wall/ceiling cut-in, column faces, mantel surfaces, built-in interiors. Also used for touch-up/detail with spray method.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5 inch) for detail
consumables.specification: 1.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle, for tight profile detail
consumables.notes: Smaller detail brush for tight profiles: wainscot rail-stile joints, panel recess corners, fluted column channels, ornate mantel molding, built-in dado joints. Used regardless of primary application method -- detail areas often need brush touch-up after spray.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup -- keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state. One brush covers ~100 SF of specialty surface before replacement.

consumables.name: Mini roller (4-inch, microfiber or foam)
consumables.specification: 4-inch mini roller frame with foam or microfiber cover
consumables.notes: Roll and Tip method for flat surfaces per FFD SS15.6: wainscot flat panels, wood wall flat panels, mantel shelf top, column flat faces, built-in shelf faces. Apply with mini roller, then tip with brush for leveling. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-411 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.011 orifice) for fine-finish millwork
consumables.notes: Fine-finish spray tips for specialty surfaces. Tight fan pattern for detail work. Multiple passes at different angles for beam undersides, column profiles, and built-in compartment interiors. One tip per ~50 SF of spray work. Replace when pattern degrades.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe surfaces immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine. One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of specialty surface. Use before every coat. Work into profile detail -- beadboard grooves, panel crevices, column channels, built-in corners trap sanding dust.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: RP caulk assess/replace at surface-to-wall junctions and internal joints. RP caulking is selective -- assess existing caulk, replace only failed sections (cracked, separated, discolored). Typical RP replacement: 15-30% of total caulk length. Joint types by surface: wainscot panel-to-wall, wood wall panel perimeter, wood ceiling perimeter, beam-to-ceiling/wall, column-to-ceiling/floor, mantel-to-wall, built-in-to-wall perimeter. ~25 LF per tube at 3/16 inch bead.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing defects revealed after degloss/scrape on RP specialty surfaces. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, surface defects, and small dents. RP fill is much less than NC (NC fills ALL fastener holes on bare wood; RP only patches damage areas). One quart per ~100 SF of affected surface.

consumables.name: Wood Hardener / Consolidant
consumables.specification: Penetrating wood consolidant, Minwax Wood Hardener or equivalent
consumables.notes: For moisture-damaged specialty surfaces where wood substrate is softened. Penetrating consolidant stabilizes wood fibers before filling/priming. Primary targets: wood ceiling in bathrooms (moisture damage at panel edges), built-in shelf edges in humid rooms, wood wall panel bottoms. One pint treats ~50 SF of affected area. Conditional on SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE + soft substrate finding during assessment.

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle to defects and scrape edges. Flexible blade for flush fill. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Paint scraper (multi-width)
consumables.specification: Rigid paint scraper, 2-inch and 4-inch, carbide or steel blade
consumables.notes: For scraping failing/peeling paint on specialty surfaces. 4-inch for flat surfaces (wainscot flat panels, shelf faces). 2-inch for detail areas (column faces, mantel surfaces). Condition-gated: FAIR and POOR only. One set per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Multi-use protection tape: wall masking above wainscot (spray), wall/ceiling masking at panel junctions (spray), fixture masking, attaching masking paper, edge masking at specialty-to-adjacent-surface junctions. 180 LF (60 yards) per roll per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Wall/ceiling surface masking at specialty surface junctions during spray application. Paper + tape system. 12-inch width covers adjacent surface area at element-to-wall, wainscot-to-wall-above, panel-to-ceiling junctions. Spray method only -- brush method uses tape line only.

consumables.name: Safe-release masking tape
consumables.specification: Low-tack safe-release masking tape, 1-inch width
consumables.notes: Low-tack tape for masking near finished surfaces that could be damaged by standard tape: stone/brick fireplace surround near mantel, delicate wallpaper above wainscot, finished countertop near built-in. Protects adjacent surface from paint contact without damaging surface finish.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft runner or 4x5 ft compact
consumables.notes: Floor protection at specialty surface work area. Runner-style at work perimeter for brush method drip containment. RP always has finished floors -- floor protection is mandatory. Shared across all surface types in the room. 1-2 per painter, reusable.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.specification: 4 mil plastic sheeting for floor/wall/furniture protection during spray
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for spray overspray and ceiling work drip risk. Also used for furniture protection in occupied homes and lightweight cover over door openings during ceiling spray. Heavier weight (4 mil) prevents tear during work. Shared across all surface types.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting lightweight (1-2 mil)
consumables.specification: 1-2 mil plastic sheeting for built-in contents covering and fixture bagging
consumables.notes: RP-specific: lightweight plastic for built-in contents protection (covering remaining items when owner has not fully emptied), fixture bagging near spray work, and opening covers during ceiling spray. Per opening with size-tier adjustment for built-in contents covering.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: Required for cleaning brushes and tools used with shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. One quart per project. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

floor_perimeter.description: Perimeter drop cloth runners at specialty surface work area for brush method drip containment
floor_perimeter.notes: Standard brush method floor protection. Shared across all surface types in the room. Upgrades to floor_full when spray method or ceiling work present.

floor_full.description: Full floor coverage for spray overspray and ceiling work drip risk
floor_full.notes: Full floor rosin paper or plastic sheeting. Triggered by spray method OR ceiling work present (ceiling drip risk). Shared across all surface types. ~10-15 min setup per room.

wall_mask_above_wainscot.description: Wall masking above wainscot cap rail during spray application
wall_mask_above_wainscot.notes: Paper from cap rail up 24-36 inches. Prevents overspray drift onto wall above wainscot.

wall_upper_band.description: Upper wall masking during ceiling spray application
wall_upper_band.notes: Paper/plastic masking on wall surface from ceiling line down 12-18 inches during ceiling spray.

ceiling_mask.description: Ceiling masking during wall panel spray (only if ceiling NOT in scope)
ceiling_mask.notes: Ceiling masking only needed when wall panels are sprayed but ceiling is NOT in scope. If ceiling is also being painted, ceiling goes first -- no masking needed.

fixture_covers.description: Light fixture, switch, outlet, and vent masking/removal
fixture_covers.notes: Per fixture count. Shared across all surface types. Bag or tape-cover each fixture.

opening_cover_lightweight.description: Lightweight cover over door openings during ceiling spray to prevent overspray migration
opening_cover_lightweight.notes: Poly sheeting or paper over door openings. Prevents overspray from migrating to adjacent rooms during ceiling spray.

builtin_contents_cover.description: RP-specific: cover remaining items in built-in if owner did not fully empty
builtin_contents_cover.notes: Poly sheeting per opening with size-tier rate adjustment (XL openings contain more items). Optional -- preferred scope assumption is owner empties built-in before painter arrives.

fireplace_surround_mask.notes: Low-tack tape at mantel junction with stone/brick/tile fireplace surround. Protects surround from paint contact without damaging surface.

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Scuff sand primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac seals stains and is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Universal undercoat.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew-resistant primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex-based mildew primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Bonding primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Designed as universal bridge coat for stain/clear conversion.

primer_selection_matrix.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: NO primer (skip-prime) when adhesion test passes on low-sheen latex. SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT when adhesion marginal, high-sheen, or oil-based existing coating.
primer_selection_matrix.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT -- spot or full depending on scrape extent.
primer_selection_matrix.SS_INT_PEELING: SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT -- full surface after complete scrape.
primer_selection_matrix.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT -- after biocide treatment and drying.
primer_selection_matrix.SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE: SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT (shellac BIN) -- full surface, no exceptions.

compatibility_rules.notes: Core RP logic: primer selection is driven by substrate state, not substrate material. Each surface type has independent substrate state allowing different primers in the same room.

compatibility_rules.description: Stain/clear coat conversion requires bonding primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Stain/clear coat conversion to paint requires bonding primer -- no skip-prime option. After first topcoat, inspect for tannin bleed-through from high-tannin species (oak, mahogany, cedar). If bleed-through, apply shellac spot-prime (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) before second topcoat.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker for smoke damage on all surface types
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac is the ONLY reliable seal for smoke/nicotine contamination. Latex and acrylic stain blockers have ZERO stain blocking capability for smoke (RC-002). Full surface application -- no spot treatment.

compatibility_rules.description: Sheen/QT gate per Fine Finish Doctrine
compatibility_rules.notes: Gloss requires QT5 prep (FFD SS4.1). Semi-gloss requires QT4+ prep. Eggshell is valid for ceiling surfaces and built-in interiors at any tier (lower scrutiny) but is not in the sheen gate -- estimator may recommend based on surface type.

compatibility_rules.description: Overhead penalty for ceiling surfaces is rate-based not modifier-based
compatibility_rules.notes: Ceiling overhead penalty (0.70-0.80x of equivalent wall rates) is baked into per-task base rates following NC production.json convention. NOT applied as a modifier. Height modifier for ceilings (H1-H4) applies ON TOP of the already-reduced overhead rate. Materials Manager note: ceiling coverage is ~5-10% lower than wall coverage for the same reason (overhead application difficulty).

compatibility_rules.description: Built-in door/drawer cure time before closure
compatibility_rules.notes: Minimum 5-7 day cure for waterborne alkyd (QT4+) before closing built-in doors per FFD SS15.11.3. Keep doors propped open during cure. Plan painting schedule to allow cure time. Applies identically in RP and NC.

compatibility_rules.description: QT5 + POOR condition gates to hourly rate (QT6)
compatibility_rules.notes: QT5 on POOR condition surfaces (peeling, moisture, smoke) is extremely labor-intensive. The combination of maximum quality expectations + maximum remediation may exceed reasonable per-unit estimation. Flag for estimator review -- hourly rate (QT6) recommended for QT5+POOR combinations.

compatibility_rules.description: Biocide treatment gate for moisture damage
compatibility_rules.notes: CON_BIOCIDE_SOLUTION treatment must be completed and fully dried (24+ hrs) BEFORE mildew primer application. Gate condition: active moisture source must be resolved by other trades before painting begins. MC > 15% is a STOP condition.

risk_notes.topic: Oil-based existing coating on specialty millwork
risk_notes.risk: Interior specialty millwork (wainscot, mantels, columns, built-ins, wood walls) historically received oil-based paint. Latex over un-primed oil-based coating will delaminate.
risk_notes.mitigation: Always perform coating ID test (solvent rub with mineral spirits) during assessment on EACH surface type present -- different surfaces may have different coating histories (built-ins repainted with latex while original wainscot retains alkyd). If alkyd identified, adhesion primer is mandatory.

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed-through on stain/clear coat conversion
risk_notes.risk: Wood species with high tannin content (oak, mahogany, cedar) bleed yellow-brown discoloration through standard latex primer and topcoat when converting from stain/clear to paint.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_BONDING for conversion. After first topcoat, inspect for tannin bleed-through. If present, apply shellac spot-prime (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) over affected areas before second topcoat.

risk_notes.topic: Smoke stain bleed-through on textured specialty surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Nicotine/soot migrates through latex primer and topcoat. Specialty surfaces with texture (beadboard grooves, panel profiles, column flutes, mantel molding) trap concentrated contamination in detail areas.
risk_notes.mitigation: Shellac-based stain blocker (BIN) on full surface. Two coats BIN for heavy contamination. Extra attention to grooves and detail areas. Latex/acrylic stain blockers have ZERO effectiveness against smoke (RC-002).

risk_notes.topic: Modified urethane open time on specialty surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Overworking modified urethane products causes roping/brush marks on flat panels (wainscot, wood wall, shelf faces) and sags on vertical/overhead surfaces (columns, beams, ceilings).
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not go back and rework. Thin coats on vertical/overhead surfaces. Sand and recoat if defects remain.

risk_notes.topic: Profile loss from paint film buildup in detail areas
risk_notes.risk: Multiple coats of paint over years fill in beadboard grooves, panel profiles, column flutes, and mantel details. Each repaint adds 2-3 mils; after several repaints, decorative profiles become soft/rounded.
risk_notes.mitigation: Assess film buildup during condition inspection. If profile loss is significant, consider scraping detail areas to restore profile definition before overcoating. Heavy stripping is out of scope for this spec.

risk_notes.topic: Runs and sags on overhead and vertical detail surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Over-application on ceiling surfaces (gravity pulls paint), in panel grooves (paint pools), on column flutes (paint settles in channels), and on beam undersides.
risk_notes.mitigation: Light coats in detail areas. Lay-off strokes to redistribute pooling. Check all surfaces 5-10 minutes after application during flash time. Spray-and-backroll for ceilings per FFD SS15.6.

risk_notes.topic: Moisture damage regrowth on ceiling and wall surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Painting over moisture-damaged wood ceiling or wall panel without treating mildew and resolving moisture source. Mildew grows under paint film.
risk_notes.mitigation: Biocide treatment before any coating (CON_BIOCIDE_SOLUTION). Verify moisture source resolved. MC < 15% before painting. Use SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT after biocide dries. Active moisture is STOP condition.

risk_notes.risk: Paint overspray, drips, or sanding dust damages personal items left in built-in shelving. Occupied home risk.
risk_notes.mitigation: Preferred: owner empties built-in before painting. If items remain, cover with CON_PLASTIC_SHEETING_LIGHTWEIGHT per opening. Verify contents protection before any prep/coating work begins.

risk_notes.topic: Lead paint on pre-1978 specialty millwork
risk_notes.risk: Specialty millwork is HIGH RISK for lead paint -- wainscot, mantels, columns, built-ins were among the last interior surfaces to transition from oil to latex. Scraping/sanding generates lead-containing dust.
risk_notes.mitigation: MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT is conditional on PS_META.BOOL.HOME_PRE_1978. RRP-certified renovator required. Containment, HEPA vacuum, and wet methods per EPA RRP Rule. Pre-1978 specialty surfaces should be presumed lead-positive unless tested.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure at built-in shelf edges
risk_notes.risk: Built-in interiors accumulate dust, wax (furniture polish), and handling oils. Insufficient cleaning causes adhesion failure at edges where mechanical abrasion from book placement/removal stress-tests the coating.
risk_notes.mitigation: TSP wash (CON_TSP_CLEANER) and thorough rinse of all built-in interior surfaces before any prep work.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection follows two independent axes: (1) Primer is STATE-DRIVEN -- selected based on substrate state per surface type (adhesion, stain-block, mildew, bonding, or skip-prime). (2) Finish is QT-DRIVEN per Fine Finish Doctrine: QT3 = SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4 = SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5 = SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Any primer can pair with any finish. Different surface types in the same room may use different primers (state-driven independently) but share the same finish system (QT-driven globally).
material_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: RP uses state-driven RP primers (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT, SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT, SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT, SYS_PRIMER_BONDING) instead of NC substrate-driven primers (MDF shellac, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood acrylic). RP primer coverage is higher than NC because previously painted surfaces absorb less. RP adds TSP wash, deglosser, assessment kit, biocide, contour sanding sponges, and wood hardener not needed in NC. RP eliminates NC consumables: wood filler (no bare-wood fastener filling), heavy spackle (reduced fill work).
material_notes.coverage_variability: Mixed UOM coverage: SF for wainscot/wall/ceiling (direct measurement), LF for beams (converted to effective SF via profile width), EA for columns/mantels (converted to effective SF via size/profile), EA for built-ins (converted to effective SF via size tier). Coverage rates are calibrated per surface type with ceiling surfaces having ~5-10% lower effective coverage due to overhead application.
material_notes.open_time_by_chemistry: Standard acrylic enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane/waterborne alkyd (Advance) has SHORT open time (5-10 min) -- do not overwork per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006).
material_notes.coat_count_summary: QT3-QT4: 2 finish coats standard. QT5 brush: 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 finish coats. Prime coat (when applicable) is always 1 coat. Shellac stain blocker: 1 coat standard, 2 coats for heavy smoke contamination.
material_notes.consolidated_protection_note: RP protection is consolidated per room -- one setup covers all specialty surface types present. Floor protection (perimeter for brush, full for spray/ceiling), wall/ceiling masking (spray method), fixture covers, and opening covers are all shared. This eliminates 12-15 redundant protection tasks from the 5 NC source specs. Setup once, work all surfaces, teardown once.
material_notes.builtin_contents_note: RP-specific: built-in contents protection using lightweight plastic sheeting. Preferred scope assumption is owner empties built-in before painter arrives. Optional add-on task if painter handles contents removal/covering.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).

assumptions.value: RP adhesion/bonding/mildew primer at 375-475 SF/gal vs NC bare-wood primer at 350-450 SF/gal
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP vs NC primer coverage differential. Derived from product PDS typical coverage range and field practice. ~5-10% higher coverage on previously painted surfaces.

assumptions.value: 250-375 SF/gal for shellac stain blocker (lower than latex primers)
assumptions.source: Shellac products have higher solids content and heavier required film build
assumptions.note: Manufacturer PDS data. Ceiling and built-in interior applications are at the low end due to application difficulty.

assumptions.value: ~5-10% lower effective coverage on ceiling vs wall for same product
assumptions.note: No doctrine quantifies material coverage overhead penalty. Parallel to the 0.70-0.80x production rate overhead penalty documented in NC production.json.

assumptions.value: ~4 SF/LF for typical residential beam (3-sided box, ~10" wide x 8" deep)
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical beam profile dimensions
assumptions.note: Beam SF equivalent varies significantly by profile: rectangular box ~3-4 SF/LF, ornate profiles ~5-6 SF/LF.

assumptions.value: ~25 SF per EA for standard 8ft column (~12" perimeter x 8ft)
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical column dimensions
assumptions.note: Fluted columns add ~30% effective surface area over smooth. Round columns have same coverage as square at equivalent perimeter.

assumptions.value: ~20 SF per EA for standard mantel (10-40 SF range based on type)
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical mantel dimensions
assumptions.note: Simple shelf ~10 SF, traditional assembly ~20 SF, ornate assembly ~40 SF.

assumptions.value: S~8SF, M~20SF, L~40SF, XL~80SF per unit including door/drawer faces
assumptions.source: BuiltIns_Shelving Quantification System v2.0 SS5 + door/drawer face estimates
assumptions.note: NC Opening Count method SF equivalents (S~2, M~5, L~10, XL~20 per OPENING) scaled up to per-UNIT because RP unit includes multiple openings + door/drawer faces. Approximate -- actual varies by configuration.

assumptions.value: 15-30% of total joint length requires replacement in typical RP scenario
assumptions.source: Research finding RF-014 -- assess and selective replace vs NC full caulk
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP caulk replacement ratio. Estimated from typical residential repaint experience.

assumptions.value: 20-30% waste for spray inside enclosed built-in compartments vs 10-20% for open surfaces
assumptions.source: Research estimate -- enclosed compartment overspray bounce-back
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifies compartment-specific spray waste.
